messages:
cleo (People Ops): quick question about vesting & contributions: someone is switching to unpaid leave on 2025-01-20 and will be back 2025-02-10. how does that affect employer 401k match and vesting service for jan/feb?

omar (Payroll): short answer: employer match is based on payroll contributions during paid pay periods. unpaid leave pay periods = no employee deferral -> no match for those checks. vesting is based on service date, not each paycheck, so short unpaid leave shouldn't break service credit unless plan has specific LOA rules.

jen (BenefitsVendor): vendor add: our system flags LOA > 30 days as potential service interruption; under 30 days we keep continuous service. for payroll, if employee makes missed contributions on return (employee catch-up voluntary), we can process as after-the-fact adjustments but taxes may change.

alex (IC): follow-up: i'm over 50 and submit catch-up contributions. can those be added retroactively if i missed a pay period while on unpaid leave?

omar (Payroll): catch-up contributions are allowed but must be entered as a payroll adjustment before the final payroll of the plan year, and some vendors require supporting doc. processing retro catch-ups after tax year-end is messy. recommend pre-authorize with payroll before returning.

cleo (People Ops): ok action items: 1) include LOA <30 days note in manager FAQ (counts as continuous service). 2) tell employees to contact payroll BEFORE their return if they want retro catch-up so we can quote tax impact. 3) benefits vendor will accept adjustment files up to 14 days after return for quick fixes.

jen (BenefitsVendor): confirm: we'll accept adjustments up to 14 days post-return for simple contribution deltas; anything older goes through reconciliation queue.

hr-bot: Reference: https://internal.redwood.com/hr/loans-contribs-vesting (internal) :link:

cleo (People Ops): i'll draft the snippet for the LOA email. Proposed line: "If your unpaid leave is less than 30 days, your service for vesting remains continuous; employer matching requires paid payroll contributions during those pay periods. Contact payroll before returning if you'd like to explore retroactive catch-up contributions."

alex (IC): perfect, thanks. i'll bookmark payroll@ and save receipts. :thumbsup:
